entities.summary: Kidinnu was a Chaldean astronomer and mathematician who made significant contributions to the field of astronomy during the Classical period. Strabo of Amaseia called him Kidenas, Pliny the Elder called him Cidenas, and Vettius Valens called him Kidynas. Kidinnu's work on the movements of the planets and the sun was widely influential, and he is often credited with the development of the first known solar calendar. His astronomical observations and calculations were used by later scholars to improve the accuracy of their own work. Kidinnu's legacy extends beyond the realm of astronomy, as his work on mathematics and astronomy laid the groundwork for later scientific discoveries. His contributions to the field of astronomy during the Classical period have had a lasting impact on our understanding of the solar system and the movements of celestial bodies. Kidinnu's work also reflects the cultural and intellectual exchange between the ancient Near East and the Mediterranean world, demonstrating the significance of the Chaldean civilization in the broader context of ancient Greek and Roman culture.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kidinnu's work on the solar calendar and the movements of the planets and the sun had a significant impact on the development of Western astronomy and mathematics, influencing later scholars such as Ptolemy and Copernicus. His legacy extends beyond the realm of astronomy, as his work on mathematics and astronomy laid the groundwork for later scientific discoveries.
